title: Gerund or infinitive after verbs
what: choosing the wrong pattern after common verbs ('I suggest to meet', 'We look forward to hear from you', 'avoid to say', 'used to working' for past habits)
summary: This error persists because it rarely impedes understanding, allowing it to become deeply ingrained. However, it subtly detracts from the speaker's fluency and precision, making their English sound less natural.
listenFor: Pay close attention to the form of the second verb when it directly follows another verb in your sentences.

contrasts.wrong: I suggest to meet early to discuss the project timeline.
contrasts.right: I suggest meeting early to discuss the project timeline.

contrasts.wrong: We look forward to hear from you regarding the proposal.
contrasts.right: We look forward to hearing from you regarding the proposal.
contrasts.note: "Look forward to" is a phrasal verb followed by a gerund.

contrasts.wrong: It's best to avoid to say anything controversial during negotiations.
contrasts.right: It's best to avoid saying anything controversial during negotiations.

contrasts.wrong: When I was younger, I used to working long hours without fatigue.
contrasts.right: When I was younger, I used to work long hours without fatigue.
contrasts.note: "Used to" for past habits is followed by the base form of the verb.

contrasts.wrong: After much deliberation, they decided going with the alternative plan.
contrasts.right: After much deliberation, they decided to go with the alternative plan.

contrasts.wrong: Despite the tight deadline, we managed finishing the report on time.
contrasts.right: Despite the tight deadline, we managed to finish the report on time.

drills: We anticipate receiving the final figures by the end of the week.

probes.sentence: The committee denied to approve the proposed budget increase.
answers: The committee denied approving the proposed budget increase.

probes.sentence: He pretended not understanding the instructions given.
answers: He pretended not to understand the instructions given.

probes.sentence: They avoided to discuss the sensitive topic during the meeting.
answers: They avoided discussing the sensitive topic during the meeting.

probes.sentence: I can't imagine to work in such a high-pressure environment.
answers: I can't imagine working in such a high-pressure environment.

probes.sentence: We failed achieving our quarterly targets due to unforeseen issues.
answers: We failed to achieve our quarterly targets due to unforeseen issues.

probes.sentence: She suggested to review the contract terms before signing.
answers: She suggested reviewing the contract terms before signing.
